sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's energy transition hinges on PLN's capex cycle and feed-in tariff revisions, making policy clarity the dominant swing factor for local renewables valuations.
US solar demand is structurally supported by IRA subsidies and grid-scale backlog, insulating SEDG/ENPH from near-term rate volatility.
Climate-tech capital is bifurcating: US equipment makers benefit from reshoring incentives, while Indonesian developers face currency and offtake risks that cap upside.
sectors.ai: US-listed renewables rebounded on rate-cut hopes while Indonesian names lagged on rupiah weakness and policy uncertainty. Buy US solar equipment (SEDG, ENPH) for near-term beta, but rotate into Indonesian utilities (HGII) only after clarity on PLN procurement and tariff reform. Hedge IDR exposure via NRG-style cash-flow names.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Premiumization and niche-brand momentum are driving outsized gains (BIKE +24.5%, POLU +18.7%) as Indonesian middle-class consumers trade up to aspirational products despite macro headwinds.
Domestic FMCG underperformance (-1.04% ID vs -0.33% US) reflects weakening purchasing power and rising input costs, favoring companies with export revenue or strong local brand loyalty.
Regulatory and distribution shifts in Indonesia are creating winners among agile, digitally-native players (AGAR, VISI) while legacy conglomerates lose share, a durable structural trend.
sectors.ai: Consumer & FMCG is in a WATCH phase with aggregate -0.80%, but the sharp divergence between ID (-1.04%) and US (-0.33%) signals local idiosyncratic stress. Rotate into high-momentum names (BIKE, POLU, AGAR) that are delivering outsized gains, but trim exposure to laggards as domestic demand softens. Prioritize exporters and niche players with pricing power over broad-market staples.

US logistics strength (CHRW, GXO) signals global trade resilience, supporting near-term IDX transport sentiment. Accumulate on dips toward support levels, targeting 8-12% upside over 3 months.
